calls.headline: Goldman sees rates held at 20% until late in the first quarter
calls.body: Goldman Sachs expects the central bank to keep its overnight deposit rate at 20% until late in the first quarter of 2027, then cut 500 basis points in 2027 and 200 in 2028, to 13%, EnterpriseAM reported from the bank's note, which Goldman's Farouk Soussa confirmed to it. It sees inflation, 12.7% in October, near 14% by December, the dollar at EGP 53 in three months and 50 in a year, and foreign holdings of local debt at about $20bn, down from about $30bn at the end of September. The note is not public; EnterpriseAM is the only outlet to report it.
calls.view: A hold into the first quarter keeps the one-year T-bill near 26% and the carry wide enough to hold foreign money even with the Fed expected to hike on December 9, which is what the pound needs into the IMF program's December 15 expiry. It also means no relief for rate-sensitive stocks before spring: developers and consumer lenders stay behind banks. Medium confidence: the path matches the October hike's message, but it rests on one bank's note.
calls.wrong: The central bank cuts on December 17, or the dollar closes above EGP 56 before the IMF board meets.
calls.notice: Reported by one outlet from a note that is not public; the view also rests on the central bank's October hike and the data log.

calls.headline: Foreigners sell and Fed-hike odds hit 97%; EGX30 drifts on thin trade
calls.body: The EGX30 fell 0.17% to 51,458.04 on Thursday and the EGX70 EWI 0.33% to 17,505.78, with 125 stocks down and 75 up, on EGP 6.24bn of turnover, the lowest in a year in the data log (Zawya, Youlyou). Foreign investors sold a net EGP 185.3m while Egyptians bought EGP 171.9m and Arabs EGP 13.4m (Zawya, About Msr). The one-year T-bill yield rose to 26.16% from 26.07%, and futures put about 97% odds on a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9 (CME FedWatch via TradingView).
calls.view: A small, orderly foreign retreat, not an exit: with the US 10-year at 5.04%, the carry on Egyptian bills is narrower, and foreigners trim stocks first. The desk expects the EGX30 to hold above 50,000 into MSCI's November 30 changes and the IMF board vote, but not to break out while turnover stays near EGP 6bn. Low confidence: thin markets move on little.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 49,500 before November 30.

calls.headline: Misr Life readies a 15% listing in December, the EGX's biggest test
calls.line: 750 million existing shares, all proceeds to the state; prospectus approval is expected early this week.
calls.body: Misr Life Insurance plans to sell 750 million existing shares, 15% of its capital, with trading targeted for early December and the prospectus due for approval early this week; retail investors get 5% to 10% of the offer and institutions the rest (EnterpriseAM, Youm7, Iqraa News). The company earned EGP 5.8bn in 2025 and targets a 70% payout from 2026, CEO Moustafa Elkamash told EnterpriseAM.
calls.view: A state sale of this size draws cash from the rest of the market in the weeks around the book, as Banque du Caire's did on October 29, when turnover already sits about 44% below its 90-day average. A well-covered book would help the state's offering program and the brokers that run it; the desk expects it to weigh on mid-caps until it prices. The 70% payout pitch competes with bank certificates near 18.75%, as Elkamash himself said. Low confidence: the price is not yet set.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes above 53,000 before the offer prices.

calls.headline: Weatherford hired to restart about 100 idle oil wells within 18 months
calls.line: A framework deal with EGPC, signed Friday, with no volume or value given.
calls.body: The Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation signed a framework agreement with Weatherford on Friday to bring about 100 shut-in wells, onshore and offshore, back into production within 18 months, using a no-rig fix chosen well by well (Egypt Independent, EnterpriseAM). EnterpriseAM puts the pace at about 5.5 wells a month, against 591 wells brought onstream in the two years to June; Halliburton signed a 50-well study on November 12.
calls.view: Each barrel produced at home is a barrel the state need not import at $92 Brent, so the program helps the fuel bill and the pound at the margin. Without a volume figure it cannot be priced yet; it adds to the case that arrears payments are bringing service firms back. Low confidence for any stock: no listed company is a party.
calls.wrong: The petroleum ministry reports oil output falling in the first quarter of 2027.

calls.headline: SEC probe report sinks Nvidia 14%; S&P 500's worst week since 2020
calls.body: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 on Friday, the Nasdaq 5.28% to 22,617.73 and the Dow 1.93% to 48,147.33; the S&P 500 and the Dow closed in correction, the S&P's seventh straight fall was its longest since February 2020, and the Nasdaq erased its gain for the year (CNN, Reuters via Business Times). Nvidia fell 14% to $125.53, erasing about $491bn of market value, after Reuters reported, citing two people briefed, that the SEC is examining its accounting (Yahoo Finance, Finimize). The VIX closed at 35.89 (Cboe).
calls.view: The report turns a valuation reset into a question about the quality of AI earnings, which is harder to buy on a dip: until Nvidia or the SEC says more, the desk expects the AI leaders to keep lagging steady earners into November 27, its open rotation view. Medium confidence: after seven straight falls and an RSI of 15 on Nvidia, a sharp relief rally can come at any time, so the test is relative.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes above 24,000 before November 27.

calls.headline: Broadcom drops 12% on a report Google trims 2027 TPU orders
calls.line: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Google is moving part of its 2027 TPU volume to MediaTek; neither company has confirmed it.
calls.body: Broadcom fell 12.2% to $304.41 after analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Google is shifting part of its planned 2027 TPU orders to MediaTek (24/7 Wall St, MLQ); TipRanks put the cut at about 20%. Neither company has confirmed it, and Goldman Sachs kept a $460 target. Marvell fell about 10% (24/7 Wall St). Broadcom's AI chip revenue grew 221% in its fiscal third quarter.
calls.view: A survey-based analyst note is not an order book, but it hits the custom-chip case at its weakest moment, with buyers already questioning AI budgets. The desk expects Broadcom to trade with Nvidia rather than recover on its own over the next two weeks. Low confidence: a denial from Google would reverse much of the fall.

calls.headline: Investors buy Treasuries: the 10-year falls to 4.92%, the VIX to 35.89
calls.line: Haven buying pulled the 10-year yield down 12 basis points on Friday, though futures still price a December hike.
calls.body: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.92% on Friday from 5.04% on Thursday (Treasury), about 20 basis points lower on the week as the AI selloff drove money into government debt (Stocktwits via TradingView), and the VIX closed at 35.89 (Cboe). Futures still put about 95% odds on a quarter-point hike on December 9, after minutes showed nearly all officials expecting one (CME FedWatch, per the newsletter's recap).
calls.view: Lower yields here come from fear, not from a softer Fed: the hike is still priced. The desk expects that to help housing and small caps less than the yield move suggests, until Wednesday's PCE release shows whether the Fed's case holds. Low confidence: a soft PCE print would pull hike odds down quickly.
calls.wrong: Futures cut the odds of a December hike below 50% before December 9.

calls.headline: Global Payments jumps 9.9% on a report GTCR weighs a $50bn buyout
calls.line: Its largest shareholder is weighing a takeover valued at about $50bn including debt; a report, not an offer.
calls.body: Global Payments rose 9.95% to $91.83 after a report that GTCR, its largest shareholder with about 16%, is weighing a full takeover valued at about $50bn including debt (Seeking Alpha via TradingView, Yahoo Finance); the stock had been up about 14% during the session. No offer has been made.
calls.view: A private-equity bid in a week like this shows buyers paying for steady cash flows the market is selling with everything else, which fits the desk's steady-earner case. The desk does not expect a deal to be announced soon. Low confidence: financing a $50bn buyout with the 10-year near 5% is hard.
calls.wrong: Global Payments closes below $84 before December 31.

view.headline: The IMF deal keeps the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: The staff deal on the final review, worth up to $2.3bn, and the $3bn of planned international issues cover a trade gap that widened 60.6% in September. With the one-year bill at 26.16%, record remittances and Brent near $92, the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–55. The risks are US 10-year yields above 5%, a half-point Fed hike and a delay at the IMF board.

notes.brent: Egypt imports fuel and LNG, so Brent at $92.57, down 3.4% on the week on surplus forecasts, eases the import bill; Saturday's Houthi missiles at Riyadh have not yet traded.
notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold: the 24K gram fell 3.8% to EGP 6,240 on Saturday as the ounce dropped to $3,515.40.
notes.dxy: 103.84, little changed on Friday and near its highest since April 2025 as December hike bets held; the pound was at EGP 53.88.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite: $57,837, down 6.0% on the day and 13.9% on the week.

news.headline: Two tankers hit in Hormuz as Qatari mediators visit Tehran
news.text: Two tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, a maritime monitor said, as Iran announced talks with a Qatari delegation; US-Iran negotiations have stalled.

news.headline: Brent edges up to $92.57 but posts a third weekly loss
news.text: Buying before Thanksgiving and Iran-war worries lifted it 59 cents late on Friday; it fell 3.4% on the week as the IEA sees a surplus.

news.headline: Gold falls to a 14-month low on Fed hike bets
news.text: Gold dropped below $3,650 early on Friday as futures priced a December hike, and settled 4.6% lower at $3,515.40.

news.headline: Saudi Arabia intercepts three Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh
news.text: The second attack on the Saudi capital in three days, after a missile damaged the PIF Tower on November 19; no casualties were reported.

news.headline: Russian missiles come down in Poland; NATO calls it a grave violation
news.text: Poland said two Kh-101 cruise missiles and a drone fell on its territory during an attack on Ukraine; it asked allies for more air defenses.
